correctness.rationale: The two-product Cayley–Laplace conjugation has been algebraically reconstructed, including the factor \(ab)^{-\alpha/2}\), the positive exponent difference \(2(1-a)(1-b)/b\), and all strict parameter boundaries. The scalar multiplier has exact essential norm equal to its supremum on the nonatomic \(L^2\) space, attained at \(t_*=\log(c_2/c_1)/(c_2-c_1)\). Off the diagonal, the full power norms satisfy \(B^n q^{-\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor}\), so zero spectral radius is proved analytically rather than inferred from finite experiments. On the diagonal, the multiplier essential range is the full interval. No unproved computational or external lemma is critical.

value.rationale: Motivated by the explicit singular-weight gap of the 2026 product-operator results and the known commutator compactness problem, the theorem calculates the exact noncompactness obstruction and completely resolves a striking spectral dichotomy on a natural two-parameter affine boundary-contact family: positive interval versus nonzero quasinilpotent Calkin image. This separates essential norm from spectral radius and supplies an orbit-damping explanation, not merely a routine special-case bound.
